chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Sa'd ibn Abi Khalaf, who said:

I said to Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him): 'I had bought a slave girl secretly from my wife, and that reached her, so she went out from my house and refused to return to my house. So I went to her in the house of her family, and I said to her:
That which has reached you is false, and the one who brought this to you is your enemy, intending to cause separation between us.

She said: 'By Allah, there will never be goodness between me and you ever, until you swear to me by freeing every slave girl you own, and by giving your wealth in charity, if you have bought a slave girl and she is in your possession today.'
So I swore to her with that, and she made me repeat the oath and said to me: 'So say,
I said to her: 'Every slave girl of mine at this moment, so she is free.'
And I had separated from my slave girl and intended to free her and marry her for my desire regarding her.

He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is nothing upon you regarding what she made you swear, and know that neither freeing nor charity is valid except what is intended by it is the Face of Allah and His Reward.'
ai.seo_question: Does an oath to free slaves or give charity require the intention to be purely for Allah's sake to be valid?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the Shia juristic distinction between the validity of an oath (yamin) and the validity of the act sworn upon (ibadah), a key principle in Usul al-Fiqh. The Imam clarifies that while the oath remains binding even if the intention (niyyah) is merely to please the wife rather than for Allah's sake, the subsequent emancipation or charity only counts as a religiously valid act if performed with the specific intention of seeking Allah's reward. This highlights the nuance in Shia scholarship where the mechanical validity of a vow does not automatically confer spiritual merit to the associated action.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Sa’ad Bin Abu Khalaf who said,

‘I said to Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup>, ‘I had bought a slave girl secretly from my wife, and that reached her. So he went out from my house and refuses to come back to my house. So I went to her in the house of her family, so I said to her,
‘That which has reached you is false, and those who came to you with this are your enemies intending to cause separation for you’.

So she said, ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! There is never going to be goodness between me and you, ever until you swear an oath with the freeing of every slave girl of your, and with the giving of your wealth in charity, if you have bought a slave girl and she in your possession today’.
So I swore an oath for her with that, and made me repeat the oath and said to me, ‘So say, ‘Every slave girl of mine at the moment, so she is hereby free’. So I said if to her,
‘Every slave girl of mine at the moment, so she is hereby free’.
So I relinquished my slave girl and had thought that I would free her and marry her for my desire with regards to her’.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is nothing upon you with regards to what you have sworn upon, and know that it is not allowed, neither the freeing of a slave nor charity until what is intended by it is the Face of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and His<sup>azwj</sup> Reward’.
en.sarwar: 18. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from Sa‘d ibn abu Khalaf who has narrated the following:

“I once said to abu al-Hassan, Musa, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, that I had bought a slave-girl secretly because of my wife and when she found out she went out of my home and refused to come back. I met her in the house of her people and said that what she has heard is false and the person who has told her is her enemy who wants to remove her from home.

She said, ‘No, by Allah there will never be anything good between me and you until you swear to free all slave-girls that belong to you and give all of your assets in charity if you have bought something. You must free a slave-girl that still belongs to you.’
I took an oath as she asked and she made me repeat the oath and say, ‘Every slave-girl that belongs to me at this hour is free,’ and I said just as she had asked.
I thought to free and then marry her because I love her.’

He (the Imam) said, ‘You do not owe anything because of your oath and you must take notice that to free a slave or charity is not valid unless it is for the sake of Allah and for the reward from Him.’”
